# Metrics definition: UX metrics and KPIs that connect design decisions to outcomes

Curated by Skill Harbor — @owl-listener's metrics-definition UX skill: help teams define metrics that connect design work to measurable outcomes. Covers four metric categories (behavioral — task completion, time on task, error rate, feature adoption; attitudinal — SUS, NPS, CSAT, perceived ease of use; business — conversion, retention, support volume, onboarding completion; engagement — DAU/MAU, session duration, feature discovery, return visits), the HEART framework (Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task success), a metric template (name, definition, method, data source, target, frequency, owner), and best practices (choose 3-5 primary metrics, balance behavioral and attitudinal, set baselines before measuring change, connect metrics to design hypotheses, report alongside qualitative insights). Honest caveats: methodology only, no tooling; for presenting the results afterwards it points to a `design-impact-reporting` skill that is not bundled here. MIT licensed. Sibling skills from the same repo are listed separately: « owl-listener-designer-skills-competitive-analysis » and « owl-listener-designer-skills-error-handling-ux ». Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
